sanskrit: jananīṣu ca vartante ye na samyag yudhiṣṭhira sadevakeṣu lokeṣu ye na vartanti mānavāḥ
english: And there are those, Yudhiṣṭhira, who do not conduct themselves rightly toward their mothers, and men who do not walk uprightly in the worlds together with their gods.

sanskrit: tena jñānena vijñāya gatiṃ cāśubhakarmaṇām tiryagyonigatānāṃ ca vijñāya gatayaḥ pṛthak
english: By that knowledge having discerned the destiny of those whose deeds are evil, and having discerned, one by one, the courses of those fallen into the wombs of beasts—

sanskrit: vedavādāṃs tathā citrān ṛtūnāṃ paryayāṃs tathā kṣayaṃ saṃvatsarāṇāṃ ca māsānāṃ prakṣayaṃ tathā
english: the manifold doctrines of the Vedas, and likewise the rotations of the seasons, the wasting away of the years, and the wearing down of the months,

sanskrit: pakṣakṣayaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā divasānāṃ ca saṃkṣayam kṣayaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca candrasya dṛṣṭvā pratyakṣatas tathā
english: having beheld the passing of the fortnights and the dwindling of the days, and having seen with his own eyes the waning and the waxing of the moon,

sanskrit: vṛddhiṃ dṛṣṭvā samudrāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ teṣāṃ tathā punaḥ kṣayaṃ dhanānāṃ ca tathā punar vṛddhiṃ tathaiva ca
english: having seen the rising of the seas and again their ebbing, and the loss of riches and again likewise their increase,

sanskrit: saṃyogānāṃ kṣayaṃ dṛṣṭvā yugānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ kṣayaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā śailānāṃ kṣayaṃ ca saritāṃ tathā
english: having beheld the dissolution of unions and, above all, of the ages, and having seen the crumbling of the mountains and likewise the drying of the rivers,

sanskrit: varṇānāṃ ca kṣayaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣayāntaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ jarāmṛtyuṃ tathā janma dṛṣṭvā duḥkhāni caiva ha
english: having seen the decline of the orders and, again and again, the end that decay leads to, and having beheld old age and death and birth and all sorrows,

sanskrit: dehadoṣāṃs tathā jñātvā teṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ ca tattvataḥ dehaviklavatāṃ caiva samyag vijñāya bhārata
english: having known the body's defects and their suffering as it truly is, and having rightly understood the body's frailty, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: ātmadoṣāṃś ca vijñāya sarvān ātmani saṃśritān svadehād utthitān gandhāṃs tathā vijñāya cāśubhān
english: and having discerned all the faults of the self that lodge within the self, and having understood the foul odors that rise from one's own body—

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kān svagātrodbhavān doṣān paśyasy amitavikrama etan me saṃśayaṃ kṛtsnaṃ vaktum arhasi tattvataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What faults arising from one's own limbs do you see, O man of measureless valor? This whole doubt of mine you ought to resolve for me truly.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca pañca doṣān prabho dehe pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ mārgajñāḥ kāpilāḥ sāṃkhyāḥ śṛṇu tān arisūdana
english: Bhīṣma said: Five faults in the body, O lord, the wise declare—the Sāṃkhyas, followers of Kapila, who know the path. Hear of them, O slayer of foes.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhau bhayaṃ nidrā pañcamaḥ śvāsa ucyate ete doṣāḥ śarīreṣu dṛśyante sarvadehinām
english: Desire and anger, fear, sleep, and breath as the fifth—so it is called. These faults are seen in the bodies of all embodied beings.

sanskrit: chindanti kṣamayā krodhaṃ kāmaṃ saṃkalpavarjanāt sattvasaṃśīlanān nidrām apramādād bhayaṃ tathā chindanti pañcamaṃ śvāsaṃ laghvāhāratayā nṛpa
english: By forbearance they cut off anger, desire by the renouncing of resolve, sleep by the cultivation of purity, and fear by vigilance; and the fifth, breath, they cut off by lightness of diet, O king.

sanskrit: guṇān guṇaśatair jñātvā doṣān doṣaśatair api hetūn hetuśataiś citraiś citrān vijñāya tattvataḥ
english: Knowing the virtues by hundreds of virtues, and the faults too by hundreds of faults, having truly discerned the manifold causes by their hundreds of varied causes,

sanskrit: apāṃ phenopamaṃ lokaṃ viṣṇor māyāśatair vṛtam cittabhittipratīkāśaṃ nalasāram anarthakam
english: having seen this world as like the foam upon the waters, wrapped in the hundredfold illusions of Viṣṇu, resembling a painting on the wall of the mind, hollow as a reed's pith and devoid of worth,

sanskrit: tamaḥ śvabhranibhaṃ dṛṣṭvā varṣabudbudasaṃnibham nāśaprāyaṃ sukhād dhīnaṃ nāśottaram abhāvagam rajas tamasi saṃmagnaṃ paṅke dvipam ivāvaśam
english: having seen it like a pit of darkness, like a bubble of the rain, all but perishing, void of happiness, ending in ruin, sunk in nonbeing, with rajas drowned in tamas, helpless as an elephant mired in mud,

sanskrit: sāṃkhyā rājan mahāprājñās tyaktvā dehaṃ prajākṛtam jñānajñeyena sāṃkhyena vyāpinā mahatā nṛpa
english: the Sāṃkhyas, O king, of vast wisdom, casting off the body fashioned for procreation, by the all-pervading and mighty Sāṃkhya whose object is knowledge and the knowable, O king—

sanskrit: rājasān aśubhān gandhāṃs tāmasāṃś ca tathāvidhān puṇyāṃś ca sāttvikān gandhān sparśajān dehasaṃśritān chittvāśu jñānaśastreṇa tapodaṇḍena bhārata
english: the impure odors born of rajas, those of like kind born of tamas, and the holy odors born of sattva, all sprung from contact and lodged in the body—these they swiftly sever with the sword of knowledge and the rod of austerity, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato duḥkhodakaṃ ghoraṃ cintāśokamahāhradam vyādhimṛtyumahāgrāhaṃ mahābhayamahoragam
english: Then this fearful flood whose water is sorrow, whose great pools are anxiety and grief, whose mighty crocodiles are disease and death, whose great serpent is terror,

sanskrit: tamaḥkūrmaṃ rajomīnaṃ prajñayā saṃtaranty uta snehapaṅkaṃ jarādurgaṃ sparśadvīpam ariṃdama
english: whose tortoise is darkness, whose fish is passion, whose mire is affection, whose fastness is old age, whose island is the sense of touch—they cross over by wisdom, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: karmāgādhaṃ satyatīraṃ sthitavratam idaṃ nṛpa hiṃsāśīghramahāvegaṃ nānārasamahākaram
english: whose abyss is action, whose shore is truth, whose firmness is steadfast vows, O king, whose swift mighty current is violence, whose great mines are the manifold tastes,

sanskrit: nānāprītimahāratnaṃ duḥkhajvarasamīraṇam śokatṛṣṇāmahāvartaṃ tīkṣṇavyādhimahāgajam
english: whose great jewels are the manifold delights, whose driving wind is the fever of sorrow, whose great whirlpool is grief and craving, whose great elephant is keen disease,

sanskrit: asthisaṃghātasaṃghāṭaṃ śleṣmaphenam ariṃdama dānamuktākaraṃ bhīmaṃ śoṇitahradavidrumam
english: whose raft is the frame of joined bones, whose foam is phlegm, O subduer of foes, whose pearl-mine is charity, fearful, whose coral is the pool of blood,

sanskrit: hasitotkruṣṭanirghoṣaṃ nānājñānasudustaram rodanāśrumalakṣāraṃ saṅgatyāgaparāyaṇam
english: whose roar is laughter and outcry, hard to cross by reason of its manifold lore, whose brine is the impurity of weeping and tears, whose haven is the renunciation of attachments,

sanskrit: punar ājanmalokaughaṃ putrabāndhavapattanam ahiṃsāsatyamaryādaṃ prāṇatyāgamahormiṇam
english: whose surging tide is the round of births again and again, whose cities are sons and kinsfolk, whose bounding shore is non-violence and truth, whose great billow is the giving up of life,

sanskrit: vedāntagamanadvīpaṃ sarvabhūtadayodadhim mokṣaduṣprāpaviṣayaṃ vaḍavāmukhasāgaram
english: whose isle of refuge is the attainment of the Vedānta, whose ocean is compassion for all beings, whose hard-won goal is liberation, vast as the sea that holds the mare's-mouth fire—

sanskrit: taranti munayaḥ siddhā jñānayogena bhārata tīrtvā ca dustaraṃ janma viśanti vimalaṃ nabhaḥ
english: this the perfected sages cross by the discipline of knowledge, O Bhārata, and having crossed the hard passage of birth they enter the stainless firmament.

sanskrit: tatas tān sukṛtīn sāṃkhyān sūryo vahati raśmibhiḥ padmatantuvad āviśya pravahan viṣayān nṛpa
english: Then the Sun bears those well-doing Sāṃkhyas upward by his rays, entering them as through the fibre of a lotus stalk and bearing them past the realms of sense, O king.

sanskrit: tatra tān pravaho vāyuḥ pratigṛhṇāti bhārata vītarāgān yatīn siddhān vīryayuktāṃs tapodhanān
english: There the bearing wind, Pravaha, receives them, O Bhārata—those ascetics free from passion, perfected, endowed with vigor, rich in austerity.

sanskrit: sūkṣmaḥ śītaḥ sugandhī ca sukhasparśaś ca bhārata saptānāṃ marutāṃ śreṣṭho lokān gacchati yaḥ śubhān sa tān vahati kaunteya nabhasaḥ paramāṃ gatim
english: Subtle, cool, sweet-scented, and pleasant to the touch, O Bhārata, the best of the seven winds, which travels to the blessed worlds—that wind bears them, O son of Kuntī, to the supreme goal beyond the sky.

sanskrit: nabho vahati lokeśa rajasaḥ paramāṃ gatim rajo vahati rājendra sattvasya paramāṃ gatim
english: The sky bears them, O lord of the world, to the supreme goal that is rajas; rajas bears them, O king of kings, to the supreme goal that is sattva;

sanskrit: sattvaṃ vahati śuddhātman paraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum prabhur vahati śuddhātmā paramātmānam ātmanā
english: sattva bears them, O pure of soul, to the supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa; and the Lord, pure-souled, bears them by his own self to the Supreme Self.

sanskrit: paramātmānam āsādya tadbhūtāyatanāmalāḥ amṛtatvāya kalpante na nivartanti cābhibho paramā sā gatiḥ pārtha nirdvaṃdvānāṃ mahātmanām
english: Having reached the Supreme Self, become stainless with their abode in that Being, they are fitted for immortality and do not return, O mighty one. That is the supreme goal, O Pārtha, of the great souls who are beyond the pairs of opposites.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sthānam uttamam āsādya bhagavantaṃ sthiravratāḥ ājanmamaraṇaṃ vā te smaranty uta na vānagha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Having reached that highest station, the Blessed One, do those of steadfast vows remember their births and deaths, or do they not, O sinless one?

sanskrit: yad atra tathyaṃ tan me tvaṃ yathāvad vaktum arhasi tvad ṛte mānavaṃ nānyaṃ praṣṭum arhāmi kaurava
english: What herein is the truth, that you ought to tell me as it is; for apart from you there is no other man whom I should ask, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: mokṣadoṣo mahān eṣa prāpya siddhiṃ gatān ṛṣīn yadi tatraiva vijñāne vartante yatayaḥ pare
english: This would be a grave flaw in liberation—if the seers who have won perfection, and the highest ascetics, still dwell upon that very knowledge.

sanskrit: pravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ dharmaṃ paśyāmi paramaṃ nṛpa magnasya hi pare jñāne kiṃ nu duḥkhataraṃ bhavet
english: I deem the dharma marked by active engagement the highest, O king; for to one immersed in the supreme knowledge, what could be more painful than such remembering?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yathānyāyaṃ tvayā tāta praśnaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ susaṃkaṭaḥ buddhānām api saṃmohaḥ praśne 'smin bharatarṣabha atrāpi tattvaṃ paramaṃ śṛṇu samyaṅ mayeritam
english: Bhīṣma said: Rightly, my son, have you asked a most difficult question; even the awakened are bewildered in this matter, O bull of the Bhāratas. Yet hear herein the supreme truth, well set forth by me.

sanskrit: buddhiś ca paramā yatra kāpilānāṃ mahātmanām indriyāṇy api budhyante svadehaṃ dehino nṛpa kāraṇāny ātmanas tāni sūkṣmaḥ paśyati tais tu saḥ
english: There where the supreme understanding of the great-souled followers of Kapila abides, even the senses come to awareness, O king, of the embodied one's own body; those are the instruments of the self, and the subtle one perceives through them.

sanskrit: ātmanā viprahīṇāni kāṣṭhakuḍyasamāni tu vinaśyanti na saṃdehaḥ phenā iva mahārṇave
english: But once forsaken by the self, like wood and like a wall, they perish—of this there is no doubt—even as foam upon the great ocean.

sanskrit: indriyaiḥ saha suptasya dehinaḥ śatrutāpana sūkṣmaś carati sarvatra nabhasīva samīraṇaḥ
english: While the embodied one sleeps together with the senses, O tormentor of foes, the subtle self moves everywhere, like the wind moving through the sky.

sanskrit: sa paśyati yathānyāyaṃ sparśān spṛśati cābhibho budhyamāno yathāpūrvam akhileneha bhārata
english: He sees aright and feels the touches, O mighty one, perceiving as before, in their entirety, even here, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: indriyāṇīha sarvāṇi sve sve sthāne yathāvidhi anīśatvāt pralīyante sarpā hataviṣā iva
english: Here all the senses, each in its own station and as ordained, dissolve through their want of mastery, like serpents whose venom has been drawn.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ svasthāneṣv eva sarvaśaḥ ākramya gatayaḥ sūkṣmāś caraty ātmā na saṃśayaḥ
english: But overmastering, in their very own stations and on every side, the subtle motions of all the senses, the self ranges abroad—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: sattvasya ca guṇān kṛtsnān rajasaś ca guṇān punaḥ guṇāṃś ca tamasaḥ sarvān guṇān buddheś ca bhārata
english: All the qualities of sattva, and again the qualities of rajas, and all the qualities of tamas, and the qualities of the intellect, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: guṇāṃś ca manasas tadvan nabhasaś ca guṇāṃs tathā guṇān vāyoś ca dharmātmaṃs tejasaś ca guṇān punaḥ
english: and likewise the qualities of the mind, and so the qualities of ether, and the qualities of wind, O righteous one, and again the qualities of fire,

sanskrit: apāṃ guṇāṃs tathā pārtha pārthivāṃś ca guṇān api sarvātmanā guṇair vyāpya kṣetrajñaḥ sa yudhiṣṭhira
english: and the qualities of water, O Pārtha, and the qualities of earth as well—pervading all these qualities with his whole being, he is the Knower of the Field, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: ātmā ca yāti kṣetrajñaṃ karmaṇī ca śubhāśubhe śiṣyā iva mahātmānam indriyāṇi ca taṃ vibho
english: And the self proceeds to the Knower of the Field, and the two kinds of action, good and ill, and the senses too proceed to him, O lord, as disciples to a great-souled master.

sanskrit: prakṛtiṃ cāpy atikramya gacchaty ātmānam avyayam paraṃ nārāyaṇātmānaṃ nirdvaṃdvaṃ prakṛteḥ param
english: And transcending even Nature, he goes to the imperishable Self, the supreme one whose essence is Nārāyaṇa, beyond the pairs of opposites and beyond Nature.

sanskrit: vimuktaḥ puṇyapāpebhyaḥ praviṣṭas tam anāmayam paramātmānam aguṇaṃ na nivartati bhārata
english: Freed from merit and demerit, having entered that flawless, attributeless Supreme Self, he does not return, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śiṣṭaṃ tv atra manas tāta indriyāṇi ca bhārata āgacchanti yathākālaṃ guroḥ saṃdeśakāriṇaḥ
english: But what remains here—the mind, my son, and the senses, O Bhārata—come back in due season, doing the bidding of their teacher.

sanskrit: śakyaṃ cālpena kālena śāntiṃ prāptuṃ guṇārthinā evaṃ yuktena kaunteya yuktajñānena mokṣiṇā
english: And it is possible in a short time to attain peace for one who seeks the qualities, thus disciplined, O son of Kuntī, joined to right knowledge and bent on liberation.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyā rājan mahāprājñā gacchanti paramāṃ gatim jñānenānena kaunteya tulyaṃ jñānaṃ na vidyate
english: The Sāṃkhyas, O king, of vast wisdom, go to the supreme goal; with this knowledge, O son of Kuntī, no knowledge is to be found equal.

sanskrit: atra te saṃśayo mā bhūj jñānaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ paraṃ matam akṣaraṃ dhruvam avyaktaṃ pūrvaṃ brahma sanātanam
english: Let there be no doubt of yours herein: the Sāṃkhya is held to be the supreme knowledge—imperishable, fixed, unmanifest, the primeval, eternal Brahman.

sanskrit: anādimadhyanidhanaṃ nirdvaṃdvaṃ kartṛ śāśvatam kūṭasthaṃ caiva nityaṃ ca yad vadanti śamātmakāḥ
english: That which is without beginning, middle, or end, beyond the pairs of opposites, the agent, everlasting, unmoving at the summit, and eternal—so the men of tranquil soul declare it.

sanskrit: yataḥ sarvāḥ pravartante sargapralayavikriyāḥ yac ca śaṃsanti śāstreṣu vadanti paramarṣayaḥ
english: That from which proceed all the transformations of creation and dissolution, and which they extol in the scriptures and the supreme seers proclaim,

sanskrit: sarve viprāś ca devāś ca tathāgamavido janāḥ brahmaṇyaṃ paramaṃ devam anantaṃ parato 'cyutam
english: and all the brāhmaṇas and the gods and the people learned in scripture—as the supreme God devoted to Brahman, infinite, beyond all, undecaying,

sanskrit: prārthayantaś ca taṃ viprā vadanti guṇabuddhayaḥ samyag yuktās tathā yogāḥ sāṃkhyāś cāmitadarśanāḥ
english: the brāhmaṇas longing for him proclaim him, their minds set on the qualities—rightly disciplined the followers of Yoga, and the Sāṃkhyas of boundless vision.

sanskrit: amūrtes tasya kaunteya sāṃkhyaṃ mūrtir iti śrutiḥ abhijñānāni tasyāhur mataṃ hi bharatarṣabha
english: Of him who is without form, O son of Kuntī, the Sāṃkhya is his form—so runs the sacred tradition; these, they say, are the marks by which he is known, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: dvividhānīha bhūtāni pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpate jaṅgamāgamasaṃjñāni jaṅgamaṃ tu viśiṣyate
english: Twofold are the beings here upon the earth, O lord of the earth, named the moving and the unmoving; but the moving is the more excellent.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ mahad yad dhi mahatsu rājan; vedeṣu sāṃkhyeṣu tathaiva yoge yac cāpi dṛṣṭaṃ vividhaṃ purāṇaṃ; sāṃkhyāgataṃ tan nikhilaṃ narendra
english: Whatever great knowledge is found among the great, O king—in the Vedas, in the Sāṃkhya systems, and likewise in Yoga, and whatever manifold ancient lore is seen—all of that is comprised within the Sāṃkhya, O lord of men.

sanskrit: yac cetihāseṣu mahatsu dṛṣṭaṃ; yac cārthaśāstre nṛpa śiṣṭajuṣṭe jñānaṃ ca loke yad ihāsti kiṃ cit; sāṃkhyāgataṃ tac ca mahan mahātman
english: And whatever is seen in the great chronicles, and whatever is in the science of statecraft honored by the wise, O king, and whatever knowledge there is in the world here—all that great wisdom too is comprised within the Sāṃkhya, O great-souled one.

sanskrit: śamaś ca dṛṣṭaḥ paramaṃ balaṃ ca; jñānaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ ca yathāvad uktam tapāṃsi sūkṣmāṇi sukhāni caiva; sāṃkhye yathāvad vihitāni rājan
english: Tranquility and supreme strength, and subtle knowledge, are duly set forth therein; subtle austerities and joys as well are duly ordained in the Sāṃkhya, O king.

sanskrit: viparyaye tasya hi pārtha devān; gacchanti sāṃkhyāḥ satataṃ sukhena tāṃś cānusaṃcārya tataḥ kṛtārthāḥ; patanti vipreṣu yateṣu bhūyaḥ
english: For when it falls short, O Pārtha, the Sāṃkhyas go ever and easily to the gods; and having ranged through those worlds, then, their purpose fulfilled, they descend again among devout brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: hitvā ca dehaṃ praviśanti mokṣaṃ; divaukaso dyām iva pārtha sāṃkhyāḥ tato 'dhikaṃ te 'bhiratā mahārhe; sāṃkhye dvijāḥ pārthiva śiṣṭajuṣṭe
english: And casting off the body, the Sāṃkhyas enter liberation, O Pārtha, as the dwellers of heaven enter the sky; thereafter those twice-born ones are devoted, beyond all else, to the precious Sāṃkhya honored by the wise, O king.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ na tiryag gamanaṃ hi dṛṣṭaṃ; nāvāg gatiḥ pāpakṛtāṃ nivāsaḥ na cābudhānām api te dvijātayo; ye jñānam etan nṛpate 'nuraktāḥ
english: For no going to the brute wombs is seen for them, nor a downward course, the abode of evildoers; nor are those twice-born ones among the unwise—they who are devoted to this knowledge, O king.

sanskrit: sāṃkyaṃ viśālaṃ paramaṃ purāṇaṃ; mahārṇavaṃ vimalam udārakāntam kṛtsnaṃ ca sāṃkhyaṃ nṛpate mahātmā; nārāyaṇo dhārayate 'prameyam
english: The Sāṃkhya, vast, supreme, ancient, a great ocean, stainless, of noble beauty—the whole Sāṃkhya, O king, the great-souled Nārāyaṇa upholds, immeasurable.

sanskrit: etan mayoktaṃ naradeva tattvaṃ; nārāyaṇo viśvam idaṃ purāṇam sa sargakāle ca karoti sargaṃ; saṃhārakāle ca tad atti bhūyaḥ
english: This truth I have declared to you, O lord of men: Nārāyaṇa is this whole ancient universe; at the time of creation he makes the creation, and at the time of dissolution he devours it again.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ tad akṣaram ity uktaṃ yasmān nāvartate punaḥ kiṃ ca tat kṣaram ity uktaṃ yasmād āvartate punaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What is that which is called the imperishable, from which one does not return again? And what is that which is called the perishable, from which one returns again?

sanskrit: akṣarakṣarayor vyaktim icchāmy ariniṣūdana upalabdhuṃ mahābāho tattvena kurunandana
english: I wish to grasp clearly the distinction between the imperishable and the perishable, O slayer of foes, in its very truth, O mighty-armed delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi jñānanidhir viprair ucyase vedapāragaiḥ ṛṣibhiś ca mahābhāgair yatibhiś ca mahātmabhiḥ
english: For you are called a treasury of knowledge by the brāhmaṇas versed to the end of the Vedas, by the highly blessed seers, and by the great-souled ascetics.

sanskrit: śeṣam alpaṃ dinānāṃ te dakṣiṇāyanabhāskare āvṛtte bhagavaty arke gantāsi paramāṃ gatim
english: Few are the days remaining to you while the sun keeps its southern course; once the blessed sun has turned, you will go to the supreme goal.

sanskrit: tvayi pratigate śreyaḥ kutaḥ śroṣyāmahe vayam kuruvaṃśapradīpas tvaṃ jñānadravyeṇa dīpyase
english: Once you have departed, from whom shall we hear of the good? You are the lamp of the Kuru line, shining with the substance of knowledge.

sanskrit: tad etac chrotum icchāmi tvattaḥ kurukulodvaha na tṛpyāmīha rājendra śṛṇvann amṛtam īdṛśam
english: Therefore this I wish to hear from you, O upholder of the Kuru race; I am not sated here, O king of kings, listening to such nectar as this.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣye 'ham itihāsaṃ purātanam vasiṣṭhasya ca saṃvādaṃ karālajanakasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: Upon this I shall recount to you an ancient tale, the dialogue of Vasiṣṭha and Janaka the Terrible.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭham āsīnam ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāskaradyutim papraccha janako rājā jñānaṃ naiḥśreyasaṃ param
english: Of Vasiṣṭha, foremost of seers, seated there with the radiance of the sun, King Janaka inquired concerning the supreme knowledge that leads to the highest good.

sanskrit: param adhyātmakuśalam adhyātmagatiniścayam maitrāvaruṇim āsīnam abhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Saluting the son of Mitra and Varuṇa as he sat there—skilled in the supreme science of the self and sure in the knowledge of the soul's destiny—with hands joined in reverence,

sanskrit: svakṣaraṃ praśritaṃ vākyaṃ madhuraṃ cāpy anulbaṇam papraccharṣivaraṃ rājā karālajanakaḥ purā
english: in well-articulated, humble, sweet, and unobtrusive speech, King Karāla-Janaka of old questioned that best of seers.

sanskrit: bhagavañ śrotum icchāmi paraṃ brahma sanātanam yasmān na punarāvṛttim āpnuvanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: O Blessed One, I wish to hear of the supreme, eternal Brahman, from which the wise attain to no return again.

sanskrit: yac ca tat kṣaram ity uktaṃ yatredaṃ kṣarate jagat yac cākṣaram iti proktaṃ śivaṃ kṣemyam anāmayam
english: And that which is called the perishable, wherein this world melts away, and that which is declared the imperishable—auspicious, secure, and free from ill.
